validated_results.title: Vitamin D deficiency predicts prostate biopsy outcomes.
validated_results.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
validated_results.reason: Prospective cross-sectional study evaluating serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and prostate cancer diagnosis among men undergoing initial prostate biopsy.

extraction.population: Ambulatory men age 40-79 undergoing initial prostate biopsy for elevated PSA or abnormal DRE in Chicago urology clinics

sample_size.excerpt: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OH D) was obtained from 667 men, age 40-79, prospectively enrolled from Chicago urology clinics undergoing first prostate biopsy.

effect_size.excerpt: In African American (AA) men, we find increased odds of PCa diagnosis on biopsy with 25-OH D < 20 ng/ml (OR = 2.43 [1.20, 4.94], p = 0.01). AA men demonstrated an association between 25-OH D < 12ng/ml and Gleason ≥ 4+4 (OR = 4.89 [1.59, 15.07]; p = 0.006).

p_value.excerpt: In African American (AA) men, we find increased odds of PCa diagnosis on biopsy with 25-OH D < 20 ng/ml (OR = 2.43 [1.20, 4.94], p = 0.01).

design.excerpt: The primary limitation of the study is the cross-sectional design.

timing.excerpt: Between February 2009 and February 2013, we enrolled 667 ambulatory men, age 40-79 years, from 5 urology clinics in Chicago, Illinois (3 academic, 1 public and 1 Veteran's Administration) that were undergoing their first prostate biopsy

continent.excerpt: Between February 2009 and February 2013, we enrolled 667 ambulatory men, age 40-79 years, from 5 urology clinics in Chicago, Illinois

location.excerpt: prospectively enrolled from Chicago urology clinics
